context: conveying & storage-vessel led · deep silo foundations are the long-lead civil driver; dust-explosion safety gates the bulk-flow trial

brief.intro: A silo, grain or bulk-materials terminal stores and moves bulk solids — grain, cement, ore, fertiliser, aggregates — between receiving points (ship, rail, truck) and storage silos or bins through a chain of conveyors, elevators and transfer towers. Unlike a process plant there is no chemical reaction and almost no process piping: the 'process' is purely mechanical material handling — intake, elevate, convey, store, reclaim, load out. The programme is civil-led at the front because a full silo can weigh many times its own empty weight, so deep piled or raft foundations are the longest single civil item and everything else sits on them; it then becomes structural-steel and mechanical led through the middle as conveyor galleries, transfer towers and bucket elevators go up. Because grain and many bulk powders are combustible, dust extraction and explosion protection (venting, suppression, isolation) are safety-critical systems that gate handover rather than afterthoughts. Commissioning is a bulk-flow throughput trial — running material through the whole intake-to-load-out chain at rate — not a chemical or utility start-up.

must_get_right: Sequence deep silo foundations first — they are the longest civil item and the whole steel and mechanical chain sits on them.
Treat dust-explosion protection as safety-critical and schedule it as its own testing gate, not a punch-list item.
Commission the material flow end-to-end — intake → convey → store → reclaim → load-out — as one bulk-flow trial, not system by system in isolation.
Coordinate structural-steel erection (galleries/towers) tightly with conveyor and elevator installation — steel is the enabler and mechanical cannot start until it is ready.

basis_of_planning.standard: AACE Recommended Practice 38R-06 — Documenting the Schedule Basis

sections.heading: Scheduling method & tools
sections.body: A Critical Path Method (CPM) network built in Primavera P6, developed to a Level 3 control schedule with retained-logic progress. Activities carry durations in working days; the network is calculated (F9) with no artificial constraints beyond contractual milestones. Total float is kept ≥ 0 in the baseline.

sections.heading: Calendars & working time
sections.body: Civil and structural-steel/silo erection run a 6-day week; conveying and electrical installation move to two shifts at peak to protect the critical path; commissioning runs an extended calendar once belt runs and the bulk-flow trial begin. A weather allowance is embedded in the civil calendar, especially for exposed steel erection.

sections.heading: Sequencing logic & critical path
sections.body: The driving path runs deep silo foundation & piling → silo shell erection (slip-form or bolted panel) → conveyor gallery & headhouse steel → conveyor/elevator installation → power & instrumentation termination → no-load belt run → bulk-flow throughput trial → handover. Dust control and explosion protection must complete ahead of the throughput trial since material cannot flow through an unproven system.

sections.heading: Key assumptions
sections.body: Design and vendor drawings (silo, conveyor, elevator) are frozen ahead of foundation design; ground conditions match the geotechnical report used to size deep foundations; the client free-issues no equipment; a single mobilisation; grid power is available to the site boundary by the date assumed. Any change to these invalidates the baseline dates.

sections.heading: Procurement & long-lead items
sections.body: The schedule is procurement-led at the front. The following are tracked as milestones and drive the network:

rows: Silo steel package (bolted panel) or slip-form formwork system

sections.heading: Access, resource & site constraints
sections.body: Heavy lifts (silo panels, elevator legs, tipper structures) require crane windows and clear laydown; rail-side or ship-side works may need possession windows coordinated with an operating terminal or rail operator. Skilled commissioning resources — belt-tracking and explosion-protection specialists — are shared across the chain and are a resource constraint late in the programme.

sections.heading: Risks, float & contingency
sections.body: Principal risks: deep-foundation ground conditions differing from the geotechnical report, silo-package or ship-unloader delivery slippage, and belt-tracking/interlock re-test loops during the bulk-flow trial. Schedule contingency is held before the throughput trial and before handover rather than spread thinly across activities.

sections.heading: Schedule levels of detail
sections.body: Reported at Level 1 (milestones) and Level 2 (summary) to the client; controlled at Level 3; expanded to Level 4–5 lookahead for the field — consistent with AACE 37R-06.
